children.text: kiṃ vā kiṃ nāsi yat prabho
yā yā dik tatra na kvāsi
kas+panthās+yena na prāpyas+kā ca vāk+na+ucyase yayā |
jñeyas+asi kila ke+api+ete ye tvām+jānanti dhūrjaṭe ||
smṛtyā nutyā ca dadate śambhave śam+bhave+abhave ||
tasya te nātha kāryāṇām+kas+vetti kiyatī gatiḥ ||
iti śaktilatā yasya puṣpitā pātu+asau bhavaḥ ||
namas+stutau smṛtau dhyāne darśane sparśane tathā |
krameṇa karmaṇā kena kayā vā prajñayā prabho |
ārambhe bhava sarvatra karma vā karaṇādi vā |
nirdvandve nirupādhau ca tvayi+ātmani sati prabho |
yā yā dik+tatra na kva+asi sarvas+kālas+bhavanmayaḥ |
iti labdhas+api karhi tvam+lapsyase nātha kathyatām ||
anāditve+api viśvasya bhoktre bhava namas+astu te ||
eṣa muṣṭyā gṛhītas+asi dṛṣṭas+eṣa kva yāsi naḥ |

children.translated_text: The profound course of <s>vairāgya</s> (dispassion), the supreme glory of <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge),
the highest pinnacle of desirelessness — You, O Lord, are the master of those who bear these.
You are <s>Brahman</s> even to <s>Brahmā</s> himself; of what ruler are You not the ruler?
Who knows how great You are, O You who are the auspiciousness of the world's auspiciousness?
What need is there of other kinsmen, or of friends, or of masters?
In every circumstance, O Lord, You are my deliverer from the ocean of worldly existence.
Victorious are the divine drops of nectar,
drawn by the power of <s>Śaiva-yoga</s>, capable of washing away the stain of delusion and <s>māyā</s> (illusion).
He whose splendor, the inspirer of thoughts, is sung by the <s>Gāyatrī</s> —
may that Lord also impel our thoughts onto the righteous path.
O <s>Aṣṭamūrti</s> (Eight-formed One), will You not grant us eternal abode in even one of Your forms?
Or perhaps, being pleased, You will do everything.
The true nature of things generally produces practical results,
but even Your mere name, O Lord, grants attainment up to <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).
The power by which You conceive ever-new states

children.text: śaktis+yā te tayā nātha kas+manasvī na vismitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: of this wondrous world, again and again — O Master, what wise person is not amazed by that?
To make the difficult easy, to turn sorrow into happiness —
the mere remembrance of Him alone is heroic; we remember that enemy of <s>Smara</s> (Desire, i.e., <s>Śiva</s>).
Victorious are the songs whose subject is the Supreme Lord,
by whose very name great souls are covered with the sprouts of horripilation.
If there were another being like You, O <s>Bhava</s>,
endowed with the creation and dissolution of the three worlds arrayed through the deployment of Your own powers —
You are the <s>mantra</s>, You are the one to be counseled, the counselor — who else is there apart from You?
O Lord, give me that <s>mantra</s> by which I may become Your <s>mantra</s> (devotee).
You are of the nature of light, of true resolve; You are the <s>Ātman</s> (Self), and so too am I that Self;
O Lord, is this state of being a worldly being merely a dream? And whence is even that dream in You?
That which is unbreakable, that which is not vulgar, that which is singular and logically sound —
that is the sovereignty of those who have surrendered the fruits of action to You, O Lord.
What calamity is He not capable of destroying? What prosperity is He not capable of granting?
He who is such — that beloved of ours, that god of gods, <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s> (the Bull-bannered One).
For the divine eye of knowledge, blinded by the impurity of <s>māyā</s> (illusion) and delusion,
O Master, devotion to You is the supreme collyrium for its purification.
That which is fearless, that which is full of bliss, that which is one and imperishable —
grant me that state! Come, O God, quickly — what do You wait for?
Ah, the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence) is by nature deep and terrible!
Ah, the supreme means of crossing it is none other than <s>Maheśvara</s> (the Great Lord)!
Salutation to You who have destroyed Death, the destroyer of <s>Madana</s> (the god of Love),
who bear the <s>Gaṅgā</s> on Your head, and who act in all that is fitting.
For those who seek a state even beyond sovereignty, knowledge, dispassion, and <s>dharma</s>,
O Master, what other supreme refuge is there apart from You?
When You are unwilling, O <s>Śambhu</s>, who has the power to bend even a blade of grass?
But one favored by Your will — who could not bear the yoke of <s>Brahmā</s> (cosmic governance)?
Those whose heads are adorned with the brilliant jewels of their crowns bowed in obeisance to <s>Hara</s> —
to what other could those rich in wisdom bow, or whom else could they not cause to bow?
Free from all disturbance, unwavering, a lake of nectar —
O <s>Dhūrjaṭi</s> (Matted-haired One), may I dwell in the midst of the ocean of knowledge born of You.
How wondrous that even when merely seen in a painting, or even when only desired in thought,
You, O Master, grant the fruit of ultimate reality in its fullness.
Who is greater than You in virtues? Who is greater than You in being beyond qualities?
Thus, O Master, we bow — should we praise You, or should we not think of criticizing? We cannot fathom.
The fruit of Your grace, which flows even from the mere recitation of the flood of nectar —
who else is able even to drink it, let alone to give it, O Lord of the world?
Since You are the treasure-house for the complete fulfillment of all that is to be desired,
from You I pray only to obtain devotion to You, O Master, by all means.
Salutation to You, the Lord of the three worlds; be favorable to those who worship You;
to the power that bestows the lordship of the three worlds without any obstacle.
When there is doubt as to what is the cause of the complete destruction of afflictions,
O Lord, having ascertained that You are that cause, who would not take refuge in You?
"Having enjoyed pleasures, having abandoned the wandering of worldly existence, I shall attain the supreme state" —
such a hope shines here only for one who has supreme devotion to <s>Śambhu</s>.
O Master, whatever I may do even in a dream, or say, whether good or bad,
through the pride of being under Your control, I am content everywhere in this.
For the mind that races toward Your abode, which is the light of all lights,
O Lord, I consider that the touch of darkness is like the younger brother of a barren woman's son (i.e., utterly impossible).
I consider that even one whose footstep is placed on the auspicious path of <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation)
has this wish standing firm: "I shall serve <s>Śiva</s>."
In the activities of sustenance, creation, and dissolution of the three worlds here,
O Lord, Your power alone is the independent instrument — You see it as self-governed.
Who in the three worlds is a protector who has not been scorched by the three afflictions?
Salutation to You who are that lake of nectar of <s>nirvāṇa</s> (liberation).
Even artificial devotion to You produces genuine fruits;
if it were without pretense, let it be told by You what its fruit would be!
That eye by which You are seen, that path by which You are reached,
that fruit, O Unborn One, which has sprung from the wish-fulfilling tree of narratives about You.
The highest good is precisely this — the abiding in You who are above all goods;
for the removal of obstacles to that, You, O Lord, are my refuge.
Ah, how supremely sweet is the nectarean flavor of the hope born of serving <s>Śarva</s> (<s>Śiva</s>),
which is ever renewed at every moment of time and never grows old!
Again and again, untiringly, through hundreds of cosmic cycles fashioning the three worlds by creative acts,
yet remaining beyond all conceptual determination — victorious is that single Unborn One.
When shall I come to stand before You, O God,
with the lamp of knowledge that burns away the wick of worldly impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>) soaked in the oil of impurity?
If You would make Your abode even for a single moment
in the mind whose faults have been destroyed, O <s>Śambhu</s>, what would You not accomplish then?
"I am blessed, I have fulfilled my purpose, I am great" — such a conviction
becomes well-founded for one whose support is You, O Lord.
You Yourself are the doer of everything, auspicious and inauspicious alike;
but devotion to You, O Lord, is the mother of the auspicious alone.
O Lord, does Your mind become clear and then You enter it, or
does it become clear because of Your entering? — thus people waver in doubt.
But the firm conclusion here is this: Your presiding over the mind
is itself the clarity of the mind, O Lord; that is the <s>siddhi</s> (attainment), that is the supreme state.
My speech, mind, action, and body, O Lord —
by Your grace, may all that become adorned solely with devotion to You.
This <s>Stavacintāmaṇi</s> (Hymn-Jewel), which grants the fruits of abundant desires,
a dwelling of the splendor of devotion to <s>Śambhu</s> — <s>Bhaṭṭanārāyaṇa</s> composed it.
